Gargzdai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Gargždai's Jewish community, dating to the 15th century, predates that of nearby Klaipėda (Memel), documented elsewhere in this collection; Memel's Jews, who had no cemetery of their own until 1823, often buried their dead here instead, and close ties between the two communities persisted even across the border separating them. The population reached 1,455 (59 percent) by 1897, mostly engaged in the timber and horse trades. Only days after the German invasion in June 1941, the Gestapo forced Jewish men to dig an anti-tank ditch and shot them the next day; women and children were killed by Lithuanians that September.
